historical_references.reference: The Han Dynasty (206 BC - 220 AD) was a major period in Chinese history, marked by strong central rule, economic prosperity, and cultural developments. Some Chinese Christians adopted the name 'Hanian' in honor of this powerful and influential dynasty.

During the Tang Dynasty (618-907 AD), there were reports of Christian communities in China, known as 'Nestorians'. Nestorians referred to themselves as 'Han-Ren', or 'Han People', reflecting their cultural assimilation into Chinese society. This influenced some European Christians to adopt the term 'Hanian' in reference to Chinese Christians.
